title: The View-Obstruction Problem for Spheres in Dimensions Six and Seven
summary: Place closed Euclidean balls of radius r at the points of (1/2, 1/2, ..., 1/2) + Z^n. The view-obstruction problem for spheres asks for the least r such that every ray from the origin into the open positive orthant meets a ball. Equivalently, it asks for D_n = sup_v min_{t in R} sum_i ||t v_i - 1/2||{Z}^2 over positive integer vectors v, where ||x||{Z} denotes the distance from x to the nearest integer. The values for n <= 5 are classical. We prove D_6 = 107/312, attained only by permutations of (12, 9, 7, 5, 3, 2), and D_7 = 73/180, attained only by permutations of (11, 10, 8, 7, 4, 3, 1). The proof reduces the supremum to a finite search. The key facts are an exact lower bound d_n(v) >= delta^2_U for every rational subspace U perpendicular to v, a matching fiber upper bound, and Banaszczyk's transference theorem, applied along the Korkine-Zolotarev flag of the dual lattice v^perpendicular intersection Z^n. The search is quotiented by signed coordinate permutations and carried out entirely in exact rational arithmetic. It terminates with a certificate: no node of the search is left unresolved, and every surviving candidate is evaluated exactly. The method also recovers the known values for n = 3, 4, 5.

title: Jacob's ladders and wander from Hardy-Littlewood integral (1918) to the $ζ$-Platonic cube form of equivalent of the Fermat-Wiles theorem
summary: In this paper we obtain $ζ$-Platonic cube form of our almost linear formula. From this follows, for example, the $ζ$-Platonic equivalent of the Fermat-Wiles theorem. The last result represents the point of contact between the Hardy-Littlewood integral and the Fermat-Wiles theorem and also with one of the Platonic solid - cube.

title: On the convexity of the fundamental domain of binary cyclotomic forms
summary: Denote by $Φ_m(X,Y)\in\Z[X,Y]$, $m\geqslant 1$ the sequence of binary cyclotomic forms, so that $Φ_m(T,1)\in\Z[T]$, $m\geqslant 1$ is the sequence of cyclotomic polynomials. We prove that, for $m\geqslant 3$, the fundamental domain $ \cal{O}_m:= \{ (x,y)\in\R^2\; \mid \; Φ_m(x,y)\leqslant 1\} $ of $Φ_m$ is a convex subset of $\R^2$ if and only if $m$ is equal to $p$, $2p$ or $2^k$ with $p$ an odd prime and $k\geqslant 2$. Finally we investigate the convexity of the fundamental domains attached to some products of binary forms $Φ_m$.

title: Novel properties of polynomials
summary: We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for a complex polynomial to have a prescribed multiset of roots, expressed in terms of its coefficients and complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials. These conditions extend the classical Vieta formulas and yield explicit formulas for the coefficients of the corresponding quotient. We apply our results to obtain characterizations of Kronecker polynomials through identities involving symmetric polynomials and construct Borwein multiples of products of cyclotomic polynomials.

title: Cohomological change of coefficients for noncocommutative Hopf algebras
summary: Let $A$ be a finite Hopf algebra over a Noetherian commutative ring $R$. For any map $f : R \to k$ where $k$ is a field, there is a natural map on the cohomology of $A$ under this change of coefficients $H^\ast(f): H^\ast(A, R) \otimes_R k \to H^\ast(A_k, k)$. In this paper we examine this map for $R = \mathbb Z[ζ]$ the cyclotomic integers with $ζ$ an $\ell$th root of unity. We show that under a finite generation assumption, the induced map gives a homeomorphism on the spectra of the two cohomology rings. Finally, we turn to small quantum groups defined over $\mathbb Z[ζ]$ and show that, with mild restrictions on $\ell$, every fiber map whose residue field has a good prime characteristic induces an isomorphism on cohomology.

title: A complete classification of minimal value set polynomials
summary: We give a complete classification of minimal value set polynomials (MVSPs), settling a problem introduced by Carlitz, Lewis, Mills and Straus in 1961. For MVSPs $F \in \mathbb{F}_q[x]$ with more than two values, earlier work showed that their value sets $\left\{F(a): a \in \mathbb{F}_q\right\}$ can be reduced to the form $\mathcal U^v=\{u^v:u\in \mathcal U\}$, where $\mathcal U$ is a vector space over a subfield of $\mathbb F_q$, and $v\geq 1$ is a suitable integer. This classification proceeds through two parallel constructions, according to whether $\mathcal U$ is itself a field or not, governed respectively by the cyclic multiplicative structure and by the additive linearized structure. In both cases, Hasse derivatives impose constraints on the root multiplicities of a distinguished factor of $F$, leading to a factorization that preserves the underlying structure in a polynomial of smaller degree and thus allows the argument to be iterated.

title: Lie (super)algebras generated by reflections in finite reflection groups of exceptional type
comment: 30 pages. The GAP code we used for the calculations is available for download as a supplementary file with this submission
summary: Using a mixture of theoretical tools and computer calculations, we describe the Lie subalgebras and the Lie sub-superalgebras generated by the sets of reflections in the group algebras of the exceptional finite reflection groups.

title: Van der Waerden's Problem for Cubic Surfaces
summary:
For a smooth cubic surface $S/\mathbb{Q}$, the absolute Galois group acts on the $27$ lines of $S_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$, giving a subgroup \[ G_S\subseteq W(E_6). \] We study the distribution of $G_S$ when the twenty coefficients of a defining cubic form are chosen independently from a large interval $[-H,H]$.
  We prove that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, the number of smooth integral cubic forms of height at most $H$ for which \[ G_S\neq W(E_6) \] is \[ O_\varepsilon\!\left(H^{19+1/21+\varepsilon}\right). \] The principal obstruction is the unique subgroup $W(E_6)^+$ of index $2$. By a theorem of Saito, membership in this subgroup is equivalent to the signed discriminant of the cubic surface being a square. A recent square-value estimate of Bonolis, Pierce, and Woo then gives the exponent $19+1/21$. For each of the other five conjugacy classes of maximal subgroups of $W(E_6)$, recent results on rational points in projective thin sets give the sharper bound $O(H^{19})$.
  We also prove the lower bound \[ N_{\mathrm{exc}}(H)\gg H^{16} \] by counting cubic surfaces containing a fixed rational line, and exhibit an $H^{14}$-sized exceptional family with no rational line, arising from rational Eckardt points. These examples lead us to conjecture that \[ N_{\mathrm{exc}}(H)=H^{16+o(1)}. \]
  Finally, we investigate whether Bhargava's proof of van der Waerden's conjecture for $S_n$ can be adapted to the index-$2$ $E_6$-problem. A double-discriminant argument gives the desired $H^{19+\varepsilon}$ bound whenever the product of the strongly square-dividing primes is sufficiently large. The remaining difficulty comes from weak square divisibility.

title: Diagrams for Roots and Quiver Representations in the context of the Gabriel-Kac Theorem
summary: Using the data of the Dynkin diagrams, we build graphical calculi for representing the positive roots of Kac-Moody algebras and the representations of quivers. Once developed, we use these to analyze the asymptotic size of the root and representation spaces, and discuss how this relates to the Gabriel-Kac theorem, the correspondence between these two structures. We give a refinement of this correspondence in terms of the trichotomy of growth rates for Kac-Moody algebras depending on if they are of finite, affine, or indefinite type, which is done in terms of what we call ``tree like" representations.

title: A Kohnen-Zagier Formula in Level 1
summary: In 1985 Kohnen used the Shimura correspondence to prove a general formula relating the coefficients of half-integral weight modular forms of level $ 4N $ transforming with respect to the theta multiplier to central values of $ L $-functions for twists of newforms of level $ N $. This generalized previous work with Zagier. In this paper, we prove a Kohnen-Zagier type formula using Yang's Shimura correspondence for powers of the eta multiplier in level $ 1 $, relating the coefficients of half-integral weight modular forms to central values of $ L $-functions for twists of newforms of level $ 6 $. To do so we develop some of the theory of modular forms transforming with respect to powers of the eta multiplier and introduce Shintani lifts of level $ 6 $, with Fourier coefficients given in terms of cycle integrals.

title: Archimedean Asai Zeta Integrals and Cohomological Test Vectors
summary: We construct explicit test vectors in the minimal $U(n)$-types of cohomological principal series representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb C)$, together with Schwartz functions, for which the Flicker zeta integrals equal the corresponding Asai $L$-factors. Both the vectors and the Schwartz functions are independent of $s$, with all normalization constants given explicitly. We construct the vectors through a polynomial realization of Schur modules. Schur orthogonality reduces the Flicker integrals to Mellin transforms of Whittaker functions, and Godement sections yield a recurrence for their Jacquet integrals. The lower-rank vectors depend on the remaining integration variables, preventing a direct reduction to lower-rank Flicker integrals. We overcome this difficulty by combining growth estimates derived from the recurrence with the Asai functional equation. This proves that the holomorphic quotient of the Flicker integral by its Asai $L$-factor is constant. An explicit asymptotic calculation shows that this constant is exactly one.

title: Determining norm-Euclidean complex cubic fields
summary: We prove that Cavallar and Lemmermeyer's list of $58$ norm-Euclidean complex cubic fields is complete. The proof combines a classical discriminant bound with exact certificates of non-Euclideanity. The unit action reduces their verification to finite lattice enumeration with rigorous interval arithmetic. An independent covering computation confirms norm-Euclideanity for the $58$ fields.

title: A finiteness result for split exceptional dual pairs
summary: We prove that big theta lifts have finite length for thirteen split exceptional dual pairs arising from the minimal representations of the split real groups of types $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$.

title: Geometric properties of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack
summary: The analytic Emerton-Gee stack is a rigid analytic moduli stack of $(\varphi,Γ)$-modules over the Robba ring, and is expected to play a fundamental role in the categorical $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence for locally analytic representations. In this paper, we establish the fundamental geometric properties of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack: it is a rigid analytic Artin stack, normal, a local complete intersection, and equidimensional of the expected dimension. As an application, our normality result removes the reducedness hypothesis in the paper of Le, Strauch, and Wang, thereby yielding an unconditional proof of the conjecture on the global sections of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack formulated by Emerton, Gee, and Hellmann.

title: An analogue of $Γ$-function for irreducible cuspidal representations of the group $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ over a two-dimensional local field
summary: Let $\mathbf F$ be a non-archimedian local field of odd residue characteristic, ${\mathcal O}={\mathbf F}[\![t]\!]\subset{\mathcal K}={\mathbf F}(\!(t)\!)$. We consider the subgroup $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})={\mathcal K}^\times\cdot{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$, and the normalizer ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm GL}(2,{\mathcal K})$ of an Iwahori subgroup $I\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$. We calculate the $Γ$-functions for irreducible special representations of $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})$ and ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})$.

title: A note on a problem of Ma and Chen
summary: Let $S=(s_1,s_2,\cdots)$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers. For any real number $α>0$, let $S_α=(\lfloorαs_1\rfloor,\lfloorαs_2\rfloor,\cdots)$. We prove that if $s_{n+1}\le 2s_n$ for every positive integer $n$, then there exists $0<α<1$ such that $S_α$ is strongly complete. In addition, this gives a negative answer to a problem of Ma and Chen in [Acta Arith. 203 (2022), 307--318]. We also prove that the same result is true if $s_{n+1}\le 2s_n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

title: Tensor products of 2-representations
summary: In this paper we define comonoidal structures on additive $\Bbbk$-linear $2$-categories which guarantee the existence of a monoidal structure on the corresponding $2$-categories of $2$-representations.

title: The Borisov--Nuer conjecture and root decompositions in even unimodular Lorentzian lattices
summary: We prove that every vector of $\mathrm{II}_{8n+1,1}$, with $n\ge1$, is a sum of two roots if and only if $n=1$ or $2$. This settles the Borisov--Nuer conjecture and implies the existence of Ulrich line bundles for every very ample polarization on a complex unnodal Enriques surface. For vectors of negative norm, we express the number of root decompositions as a Fourier coefficient of a vector-valued theta series, reducing existence to positivity. The main analytic difficulty is to obtain estimates uniform over lattices of unbounded determinant. We address this by combining a reduction based on primitive sublattices of codimension one and least determinant with explicit bounds for theta norms and Fourier coefficients of cusp forms.

title: Composition factors and finite representation type
summary: We prove that an Artin algebra has finite representation type if its indecomposable finitely generated modules are determined, up to isomorphism, by their composition factors. This gives an affirmative answer to the conjecture on composition factors and finite representation type recorded by Auslander, Reiten and Smalo.

title: Lifting mod $p$ Galois representations over local fields
summary: Let $K$ be a local field with absolute Galois group $G_{K}$ and let $k$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$. We prove that every continuous representation $G_K\to \operatorname{GL}_{n}(k)$ lifts to a continuous representation $G_K\to\operatorname{GL}_{n}(W(k))$ where $W(k)$ is the ring of infinite Witt vectors over $k$.

title: The bigraded Frobenius series of the wreath product superspace coinvariant rings
summary:
We determine the bigraded Frobenius series of the superspace coinvariant ring $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n}$ for the wreath products $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$, which is the quotient of the ring $\mathbb{C}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\otimes\bigwedge[θ_1,\ldots,θ_n]$ of polynomial-valued differential forms by the ideal generated by diagonal $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$-invariants with vanishing constant term. The bigraded multiplicity of each irreducible character is a sum over standard Young $r$-tableaux of an expression determined by the flag major index and flag descent number. This refines the Frobenius series graded by fermionic degree found by Bhattacharya--Rhoades (2026). It specializes at $r=2$ to the hyperoctahedral group $\mathfrak{B}_n$ case, and it specializes at $r=1$ to recover the theorem of Murai--Rhoades--Wilson (2025) on the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$.
  We give new formulas for the bigraded multiplicities of hook characters of the superspace coinvariant ring in types $A$ and $B$, yielding upper bounds on trigraded multiplicities of the sign character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$ and the determinant character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{B}_n}$. As a corollary, we deduce a conjecture of F. Bergeron (2024) on hook components of $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$.

title: Representations and $n$-universality of hermitian lattices over local and number fields
summary: Let $E/F$ be a quadratic field extension. For any positive integer $n$ an integral hermitian form over $E/F$ is called $n$-universal if it represents all integral hermitian forms of rank $n$ over $E/F$. We study $n$-universal hermitian forms when $F$ is a local field of characteristic $\neq 2$ or a number field. In the local case, we characterize $n$-universal integral hermitian forms and provide finite criterion sets for $n$-universality. In the number field case, we show that an indefinite integral hermitian form is $n$-universal if and only if it is $n$-universal everywhere locally.

title: The Categorical Fargues-Scholze Correspondence at Generic Parameters
summary: Let $G$ be a quasi-split reductive group over a finite extension $F$ of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We study the Fargues-Scholze categorical Langlands correspondence at generic parameters $φ$, namely those whose semisimplification does not coincide with that of any parameter with nontrivial monodromy. Extending the theory of quasi-exceptional sets on the nilpotent cone developed by Bezrukavnikov to the setting of disconnected reductive groups which arise as stabilizers of semisimple generic parameters, to any irreducible representation $ρ$ of such a group we construct sheaves labeled $\overline{\nabla}_ρ$, $\overlineΔ_ρ$, $IC_ρ$, and $δ_ρ$ on the moduli stack of L-parameters for $G$. Using forthcoming work of Hamann, Hansen, and Mann on geometric Eisenstein series compatibility, the (conjectural, in general) behavior of the correspondence at generous parameters, and the (conjectural, in general) agreement between Fargues-Scholze and classical semisimple L-parameters we prove that these sheaves correspond under the Fargues-Scholze functor to the sheaves $i_{b!}π$, $i_{b\sharp}π$, $i_{b\sharp!}π$, and $i_{b!*}π$ on $\text{Bun}_G$, where $π$ is a smooth irreducible representation with Fargues-Scholze parameter $φ$. As applications we prove t-exactness properties of the Fargues-Scholze functor specialized at a generic parameter, and that Hecke operators are perverse t-exact on the generic locus. We also construct and study foundational properties of Hecke eigensheaves at generic parameters, compute non-semisimplified Fargues-Scholze parameters on the generic locus, and construct a Fargues-Scholze-theoretic version of the BM-O bijection at generic parameters.

title: An asymptotic Jensen-Polya criterion for GRH
comment: 16 pages (extends and generalize old work by the author and others to the unshifted setting). Comments welcome
summary: The Jensen--Pólya criterion expresses the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH) for Dedekind zeta-functions as a real-rootedness condition on their Jensen polynomials. Previous asymptotic results require large shifts, while computations establish real-rootedness in the Riemann case through a finite range of degrees. Here we study the unshifted family as the degree tends to infinity. For every number field $K$, we prove unconditionally that $J_{K,d}(X)$ is nonzero and has at least $d-C_K\sqrt{d\log d}$ distinct negative real zeros for all sufficiently large $d$, where $C_K>0$ depends only on $K$. Therefore, the proportion of real zeros tends to one with error $O_K(\sqrt{\log d/d})$. The main theorems have been autoformalized in Lean~4 by AxiomProver.

title: Positivity of the Mirabolic Quantum Groups
summary: In this paper, we construct the canonical basis for the modified mirabolic quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_n$. We then study the associated $\dot{U}_v(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-module and $\dot{U}_v(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-comodule structures and prove the positivity of this basis with respect to these two structures.

title: Serre's conjectures for $\Q(\sqrt{13})$
summary: The present article proves (assuming GRH and a minor technical result) the veracity of Serre's conjectures for the field $\Q(\sqrt{13})$. In doing so, we prove a ``reduction to level 1'' result that holds for any real quadratic field with narrow class number one. However we can only establish the needed base cases for $\Q(\sqrt{13})$.

title: Comparing metric completions of triangulated categories with Verdier quotients
summary: Neeman's metric on a triangulated category assigns lengths to morphisms and allows us to construct triangulated metric completions of the category. We prove that the metric completion of a triangulated category with respect to a constant metric is always a subcategory of the Verdier quotient by the thick subcategory generated by cones of zero-length morphisms, and we provide a sufficient criterion for equality. To that end, we define continuous functors between completions which induce triangulated functors between completions. Moreover, we give two applications. First, we show that the additive equivalence discovered by Cummings and Gratz between the Paquette-Yildirim completion and a specific metric completion of an Igusa-Todorov discrete cluster category is, in fact, a triangulated equivalence. Second, we fully classify metric completions of bounded derived categories of coherent sheaves over weighted projective lines of domestic or tubular type.

title: Reciprocity formulas for generalized Dedekind character sums
summary: In this paper, we apply the Fourier series technique to establish a new formula for the product of the generalized Bernoulli function and the Bernoulli function. As applications, we derive some reciprocity formulas for generalized Dedekind character sums. In particular, we show that the reciprocity formulas of Berndt, Can, and others follow as special cases.

title: Affinizations and braided module categories
summary: We relate affinizations of braided monoidal categories to braided module categories, allowing a twist by a braided monoidal automorphism. Our main theorem establishes a bijection between twisted braided structures on a right module category and extensions of its action to the corresponding twisted affinization. We also show that the twisted affinization is the free twisted braided module category on one object. We give explicit presentations of twisted affinizations, both as monoidal categories and as module categories, using invertible dots and reflection relations. We also describe the relation to cylinder twists and tensor-pair cylinder twists, including the naturality condition needed to obtain a braided module structure. As applications, we obtain module-category presentations of the affine Kauffman and affine oriented skein categories and an orientation-reversing twisted version of the latter. We realize the disoriented skein category as a quotient of this twisted affinization by a single additional relation.

title: CA2 numbers and the Riemann hypothesis: a numerical investigation of Ramanujan's inequalities
summary: Robin's criterion reduces the Riemann hypothesis to an inequality for colossally abundant (CA) numbers, and Wu's theorem reduces the test further to the subclass CA2. We study this reduction numerically and consider smaller subsets on which the same criterion remains sufficient. We also show that the logarithmic decay law suggested by Briggs's computations follows from Ramanujan's conditional bounds. To investigate the next term, we compare the normalized Robin difference with Ramanujan's oscillatory expression involving the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. The resulting difference has a slowly varying component on both CA and CA2. Its scaled values continue to vary over the computed range, leading to questions about convergence, upper bounds, and higher-order terms. We describe the sampling used in the figures and estimate the error from truncating the sum over zeros.

title: Finite-dimensional irreducible representations of Yangians
summary: We present a direct proof of the well-known classification of finite-dimensional representations of the Yangian $Y(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ following an approach by Chary-Pressley for $U_q(\mathfrak{ \hat sl_2})$.

title: Free modules of vector-valued modular forms and applications to Jacobi forms
summary: The space $M(ρ;\mathcal{E})$ of weakly holomorphic modular forms for a dimension-$r$ complex representation $ρ$ of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ with growth prescribed by $\mathcal{E}$ at the cusp is a free module over $\mathbb{C}[E_4,E_6]$. We first prove that a $\mathbb{C}[E_4,E_6]$-linearly independent homogeneous family $F_1,\ldots,F_r$ in this module gives a basis if and only if $\sum_{i=1}^r \operatorname{wt}(F_i)=12\operatorname{tr}\mathcal{E}$. We then extend this criterion to Jacobi forms. As applications, we determine the generator weights of free modules of $\mathrm{O}(D_{8d}^+)$-invariant Jacobi forms of index $D_{8d}^{+}(p)$, where $D_{8d}^{+}$ is an even unimodular lattice extending $D_{8d}$, $d\ge2$, and $p=2,3,5$.

title: Syzygy-Quiver Formulas and Finitistic Dimensions of Special Biserial Algebras
summary:
Let $Λ$ be a finite dimensional algebra over a field $\mathbf{k}$. We introduce the reachable syzygy quiver of $Λ$, a directed multigraph whose vertices are the isomorphism classes of indecomposable nonprojective direct summands of iterated syzygies of simple modules, and whose arrows record nonprojective summands of first syzygies. The projective dimension of a vertex is one plus its directed path height, allowing the global and finitistic dimensions of $Λ$ to be read off from this height function. This formula holds for every finite dimensional algebra, but its states are arbitrary modules.
  We show that when the first syzygy of an indecomposable module admits a closed combinatorial description from the bound quiver, this state space reduces to a smaller combinatorial quiver, making the global and finitistic dimensions exact computable invariants. We carry this out in three stages. Over a special biserial algebra, the Liu--Morin closure theorem identifies the reachable syzygy quiver with a string-syzygy quiver whose vertices are string modules. Over a string algebra, this compresses to the relation-chain quiver of Xin and Zhang, recovering their global dimension formula along with a parallel formula for the finitistic dimension. Over an arbitrary biserial algebra, the universal formula holds, but uniform compression to paths or strings is impossible, with the Skowroński--Waschbüsch algebra providing a witness. Finally, we show two string algebras may share the same Gabriel quiver but have distinct global dimensions, proving the ideal of relations is indispensable for these invariants, and we prove that a pointwise homological reduction to a string algebra on the same quiver preserving the monomials of the relations is impossible.

title: Centres of mass, Steiner's theorem, and equations of Erdős-Moser type
summary: We study the Erdős--Moser equation $1^k+2^k+\dots+(m-1)^k=m^k$ and its analogue in arithmetic progressions, $\sum_{i<m,\ i\equiv b \pmod q} i^k=m^k$, by means of centres of mass, through what we call the half-mass principle. For the progression equation we show that a solution with exponent $k$ has at most $\lfloor k/\log 2+3/2\rfloor$ terms for all $k<10^{55}$, which is best possible for real solutions and replaces an exponential bound; that for $k=3$ solutions with exactly $n$ terms exist if and only if $n\in\{3,4,5\}$, and then infinitely many; and that there are no solutions at all for $k=4$, more generally for every $k=2^s\ge 4$, and for every even $k$ with $4\le k\le 24$. These results rest on a uniform estimate for the Erdős--Moser equation: the real exponent $κ_m$ for which $1^κ+\dots+(m-1)^κ=m^κ$ satisfies $κ_m=\log 2\,(m-3/2-γ_m/m)$ with $0<γ_m<1/(8\log 2)$ for every $m\ge 3$. The method also explains the constants: $3/2$ is a Steiner quotient $(ρ^2+d^2)/2d$, and $25/12-3\log 2=1/12-f''(\log 2)/2$ with $f(λ)=λ/(e^λ-1)$, which explains why this number is so small.

title: Standardly stratified structures from tilting modules
summary: Characteristic tilting modules play a central role in the theory of standardly stratified algebras, for instance in Ringel duality. They are constructed from the standard modules, which are determined by a partial order on the simple modules. In this paper, we characterize characteristic tilting modules intrinsically. We show that a tilting module is a characteristic tilting module if and only if the matrix of composition multiplicities of its indecomposable direct summands is triangular with respect to suitable orderings of the summands and of the simple modules. In this case, the standard modules and all the corresponding partial orders are recovered from the tilting module. As an application, we prove that the tilting correspondence of Geiss, Leclerc and Schröer between a GLS path algebra and its associated hereditary algebra restricts to a bijection between characteristic tilting modules. In particular, we obtain GLS path algebras that are not quasi-hereditary with respect to any partial order but for which every tilting module is a characteristic tilting module.

title: The trace distribution of $r$-primitive $k$-normal elements of finite fields
summary: Let \(q=p^e\) be a prime power and \(n\geq1\). Let \(L=\F_{q^n}\) and \(K=\F_q\). We study the trace distribution of \(r\)-primitive \(k\)-normal elements of \(L\) over \(K\). We first derive exact formulas for the number of \(k\)-normal elements of \(L\) with a prescribed trace in \(K\). For \(r\mid q^n-1\), \(0\leq k\le n-1\), and \(a\in K\), let \(\mathcal{N}_{r,k}(a)\) denote the number of \(r\)-primitive \(k\)-normal elements of \(L\) with trace \(a\). We establish a sufficient condition for \(\mathcal{N}_{r,k}\) to be constant on \(K^\times\). We also identify a subgroup \(H_r\) of \(K^\times\) and prove that \(\mathcal{N}_{r,k}\) is constant on each coset of \(H_r\). Finally, we obtain a necessary and sufficient character-sum condition for \(\mathcal{N}_{r,k}\) to be constant on \(K^\times\).

title: Parahoric Spherical Whittaker Functions
summary: Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field and let $K_μ$ be a standard parahoric subgroup of $GL_n(F)$. We express the diagonal values of normalized parahoric Whittaker eigenfunctions with trivial central character using blockwise Casselman--Shalika formulas with the appropriate modulus factor. Every irreducible generic Iwahori-spherical representation has a one-dimensional fixed space for a suitable parahoric, with no invariants under a strictly larger parahoric. The full Hecke character of this line determines the representation. We compute its adjacent-block Hecke eigenvalues and, under additional irreducibility hypotheses, obtain an explicit finite formula on every Bruhat cell using an opposite induced model, Whittaker-preserving intertwiners, and Demazure--Whittaker operators. We apply these formulas to local Rankin--Selberg integrals for $GL_n\times GL_1$ and for compatible parahorics in $GL_n\times GL_m$. In the latter case, the lowest Laurent coefficient and the equal-rank functional equation determine the integral. Explicit translations and rescalings then give test vectors for the local $L$-factor.

title: An introduction to the strategy of transcendence proofs
summary: The proof by Ch. Hermite of the transcendence of the number e in 1873 is the model on which most transcendence proofs for constants of analysis are based. The Schneider-Lang Theorem gives an opportunity to understand the strategy behind the proof. We only outline the main ideas, without providing technical details, for which we refer to the bibliography.

title: Harmonic Analysis on $p$-adic Unipotent Groups
summary:
Let $G$ be a $p$-adic unipotent group and let $H$ be an algebraic subgroup of $G$. Given a unitary character $χ$ of $H$, we consider the monomial representation $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$.
  To the character $χ$, we associate the affine subspace $$ X_χ=f+\mathfrak h^\perp\subset\mathfrak g^*$$ where $f$ is a linear form associated with $χ$. We describe the irreducible representations occurring in the central decomposition
  of $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$ in terms of the coadjoint orbits in $\mathfrak g^*$ that meet $X_χ$. We also determine the corresponding measure class on the unitary dual $\widehat G$. Furthermore, we study the multiplicities of the irreducible representations in this decomposition. As an application, we compute the Plancherel formula for $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$ when $H$ is a normal algebraic subgroup of $G$ and the multiplicities are finite.

title: On short averages of the Fibonacci partition function
summary: We show that short averages of the Fibonacci partition function over $(H, H + H^α]$ can be significantly smaller than long averages over $(0,H]$, for any constant $α\in (0,1)$. This provides a negative answer to a question that we asked in our previous work on this topic (Journal of Number Theory, 2024).

title: Induced representations from the Heisenberg parabolic subgroup of $SL(n+2,\mathbb{R})$
summary: The group $G = SL(n+2,\R)$ has a parabolic subgroup $P = MAN$ whose unipotent radical is a Heisenberg group. We study representations induced from a character of $P$, and using the Lie algebra action on the space of $K$-finite vectors we find the points of reducibility and the complementary series. We identify solutions to the conformally invariant systems of differential operators as subrepresentations.

title: Rational points of exact period three for the quadratic family
summary: For the quadratic family $f_c(x) = x^2 + c$ over $\Q$, we isolate a general $S$-unit and ABC template for rational periodic cycles: under the ABC conjecture, any rational quantity built from the consecutive-point sums of a rational period-$n$ cycle whose value and shift-by-$1$ are both $S$-units (with $S$ the support of the denominator of $c$) has logarithmic height at most $(1+\eps)\sum_{p \in S} \log p + O_\eps(1)$. Specializing to period $3$ in the change of coordinates $u = x_0 + x_1$ and $v = x_0 + x_2$, the period-$3$ condition reduces to $v = -1/(1+u)$, forcing the parameter $t = u$ to satisfy $t, t+1 \in \Z[S^{-1}]^\times$; the template then yields, under ABC, $\max\{|a|,|b|,|a+b|\} \le C_\eps \rad(d)^{1+\eps}$ for $t = a/b$ in lowest terms. We also characterize the period-$3$ locus on the $(u,v)$-plane intrinsically, isolating the ghost curve. Extending the height bound to higher periods remains an open structural question.

title: Permutation twisted cohomology, reduced and immersed
summary: In this paper, we introduce a `reduced' form of permutation twisted cohomology as introduced by Balmer--Gallauer and further developed by Miller. This ring is bigraded by a well-chosen choice of endotrivial complex, rather than multigraded by a family of endotrivial complexes. The Balmer spectrum of the small derived category of permutation modules openly immerses into the homogeneous spectrum of this ring. We also show that for $p$-groups, Miller's `remixed' twisted cohomology ring also admits the Balmer spectrum as an open subspace, and confirm in both cases it can be upgraded to have Dirac scheme structure; furthermore, we prove that the two open covers witnessing this are in general different.

title: Moments of characteristic polynomials at random matrix Gram points
summary: We evaluate the characteristic polynomial of a random unitary matrix at the points on the unit circle where the polynomial takes real values. In analogy to the Riemann zeta function we call these the ``random matrix Gram points''. On the random matrix side we answer in the affirmative a question of Richard Hall, who expected that zeta on the Gram points should be larger than typical. We prove that for any fixed positive $k$, the $2k$th moment of the characteristic polynomial averaged over the random matrix Gram points is larger than the $2k$th moment of the characteristic polynomial averaged over the whole unit circle. For large $N$ the leading-order asymptotic term is the same size, but all lower-order terms are larger. In an appendix we show how to adapt the heuristic recipe of Conrey--Farmer--Keating--Rubinstein--Snaith to conjecture moments of zeta at Gram points, and show by example that the second and fourth moments calculated by following the recipe agree with previously proven results.

title: Quasimodularity of $q$-series associated to root lattices
summary: Motivated by conjectures arising in part from the study of class-$\mathcal{S}$ vertex algebras associated with four-dimensional supersymmetric field theories, we study multiple $q$-zeta functions attached to finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras. We prove their conjectured quasimodularity for all classical Lie algebras of types $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$, as well as a more general Weyl-symmetrized version in which the exponents attached to the positive roots are allowed to vary, under a suitable parity condition. Our proof is based on a substantially more general result. We introduce new combinatorial objects, called sets of level one and pairs of level two, which generalize the configurations arising from classical root systems. To these we associate multivariable lattice sums and prove that, under a natural admissibility condition, they are Fourier expansions of polar quasi-Jacobi forms of level one and level two, respectively. Quasimodularity of the Lie-theoretic $q$-series follows by specialization of the elliptic variables. The positive roots of type $A$ form a set of level one, and those of types $B$, $C$, and $D$ are described by pairs of level two. The proof combines a structural analysis of these new combinatorial configurations with reduction procedures and induction on the rank. The resulting framework applies to a much wider class of lattice sums than those coming from root systems and supports more general quasimodularity conjectures for $q$-series associated with integral hyperplane arrangements.

title: Low-rank matrices with three prescribed off-diagonal values over $\mathbb{F}_p$
summary: Let $p$ be a prime such that $2$ is a primitive root modulo $p$. We prove that, for every three-element set $L\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p$ and every integer $n\geq1$, there exists a symmetric $n\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with zero diagonal, off-diagonal entries in $L$, and rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. This answers a question of Bukh for all such primes and, in particular, settles the case $L=\{1,4,6\}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_{19}$ singled out on his problem list. When $0\notin L$, a standard polynomial argument shows that the exponent $1/3$ is optimal. The proof combines a geometric construction in characteristic two with an incidence matrix factorization over $\mathbb{F}_p$. The same construction yields integer lifts $L'$ of the prescribed sets $L$ and symmetric $L'$-matrices of rational rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. When $0\notin L'$, this improves Bukh's general quadratic lower bound, giving matrices of order $Ω_{p,L}(r^3)$ and rational rank at most $r$.

title: An Arithmetic Property of Intertwining Operators for Real Reductive Groups
summary: Let $G$ be the group of complex points of a connected split reductive group defined over ${\mathbb Q}$. We study the standard intertwining operator between representations parabolically induced from essentially tempered cohomological representations of Levi subgroups of maximal parabolic subgroups. Under certain algebraicity, purity, and criticality hypotheses, the operator is holomorphic and invertible at a particular point of evaluation. The relative Lie algebra cohomology of these induced representations is one-dimensional in the lowest nonzero degree. Under prescribed rational generators of these one-dimensional spaces, we show that the intertwining operator is a nonzero rational multiple of a certain product of ratios of local $L$-factors. This is a cohomological version of Langlands's calculation of the Gindikin-Karplevic formula. The main theorem provides a local input for the arithmetic study of special values of Langlands--Shahidi $L$-functions.

title: Least common multiples of polynomial values: averaging, ray classes, and Galois statistics
summary: We study analogues over number fields and the probabilistic congruence input that enters averaged versions of this problem. We prove an asymptotic formula for the least common multiple of ideals in a fixed ray class, record local equidistribution estimates for random $S_n$-polynomials, and give a conditional reduction of the averaged higher degree problem to explicit dispersion and large prime collision estimates. We also formulate an individual quadratic number field analogue and reduce it to a prime ideal quadratic root equidistribution statement together with a geometric pair counting estimate. The Galois group counting input is updated using Bhargava's theorem over $\mathbb Q$ and the determinant method estimates of https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35030 .

title: Vanishing near the virtual cohomological dimension of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)$
summary:
We prove the Church--Farb--Putman conjecture that \[
  H^{N_n-i}(\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z);\mathbb Q)=0,
  \qquad N_n=\binom n2,\quad n\ge2,\quad 0\le i<n-1. \] The proof relies on Franke's filtration of the weighted automorphic cochain complex, developed in his proof of Borel's conjecture. We treat trivial and nontrivial cuspidal support separately. For nontrivial support, we combine a degree calculation with the Chenevier--Lannes lower bound of $11$ for the motivic weight of level-one regular algebraic cuspidal representations of rank at least two. This reduces the contributing inducing data to a trivial factor and a Speh factor attached to such a representation. We construct primitives for closed lifts of cohomology classes in the filtration quotients by combining an Eisenstein residue identity with a cochain homotopy and finite distributions in the spectral parameters. A finite-filtration lifting argument then yields vanishing for nontrivial cuspidal support. The trivial-support case is treated using Franke's topological model.

title: Hilbertian Fields and Profinite Iterated Monodromy Groups Over Transcendental Elements with Specializations of Infinite Index
summary: Given a field $L$ and polynomial $f(x)/L$, one can consider the indices of the profinite iterated monodromy groups formed over the ground field within the profinite iterated monodromy groups over elements transcendental over $L$. For any countable Hilbertian field $k$, we show random Galois fixed field extensions almost surely make the indices infinite over all ground field elements, with certain conditions on $f(x)$. This is a generalization of a result in arXiv:2012.03076 by Dittmann and Kadets.

title: Extreme values of Artin $L$-functions at $s=1$
summary: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ be a Galois extension of number fields with Galois group $G$. Let $χ$ be any character on $G$ and $κ(χ)$ be the leading coefficient of the Laurent series of the Artin $L$-function $L(s,χ)$ at $s=1$. Cho, Lemke Oliver, and Zaman (2026) recently established a conditional bound for $κ(χ)$ assuming GRH for the Dedekind zeta function of $K$. Up to implied constants, we show that the extremal values of these bounds are attained for an infinite family of extensions $K/\mathbb{Q}$ and all irreducible faithful characters $χ$, provided $G$ is a regular Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$. All characters $χ$ are permitted without restriction when $G$ is abelian, $A_n, S_n$, or any sporadic group. Our method removes the assumptions of GRH and Artin's holomorphy conjecture from an argument of Duke (2003) by following the strategy of Lemke Oliver, Thorner, and Zaman (2024) on the existence of extremal class numbers for number fields of arbitrary degree. Key ingredients include progress by Débes (2017) towards Malle's conjecture, and an Artin $L$-function large sieve by Lemke Oliver and Smith (2024).

title: Geometric Proofs of Riemann-Type Theta Relations
summary: We present a geometric method for deriving theta function identities from automorphisms of positive definite quadratic forms. Given an automorphism of a quadratic form with matrix $A$, we construct a rational isometry of $I_n\otimes A$ that fixes the diagonal subspace pointwise. Elementary lattice decompositions and finite character sums then yield explicit transformation formulas for the associated theta functions. As applications, we give a geometric proof of Schultz's generalization of the Borweins' cubic theta identity and recover two related quadratic theta identities.

title: Shifted convolutions of divisor functions
summary: We establish the leading asymptotic for the shifted correlations of divisor functions.

title: Multiple representations in difference sets under polynomial density constraints
summary: Motivated by the classical study of additive representation functions and the combinatorial phenomenon of sum-difference asymmetry, we investigate the subtractive representation function $d_{\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}}(n)$, which counts the number of solutions of the equation $n = b - a$ with $a\in \mathcal{A}$ and $b\in \mathcal{B}$. Specifically, we study lower bounds and the asymptotic behavior of $d_{\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}}(n)$ under polynomial density constraints of orders $x^α$ and $x^{1-α}$, where $0 < α< 1$. We first establish a general lower bound for the first moment of $d_{\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}}(n)$. Furthermore, by employing a recursive construction, we prove that this lower bound is essentially optimal under certain regularity assumptions on the counting functions. Finally, utilizing probabilistic methods, we show the existence of sets for which $d_{\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}}(n)$ has a logarithmic point-wise upper bound.

title: Petersson-rigid lattices of signature (2,1) and their harmonic weak Maass forms
comment: 43 pages, 3 tables. Paper III of a series (arXiv:2608.19706, arXiv:2609.02843). Every statement marked [C] is reproduced by a script and a log of the reproduction archive, Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23770095
summary:
An even lattice $L$ of signature $(2,1)$ is Petersson-rigid if the orthogonal group of its discriminant form acts absolutely irreducibly on the space of cusp forms of weight $\frac32$ for its Weil representation, a space of dimension at least two. We prove, with computer assistance, that there are exactly twelve such lattices up to isometry, and we determine their root bases. Four of them are theta lattices, whose cusp forms are lifts of unary theta series. On each, the space is $\mathbb C F_0\otimesσ_0$ for one form $F_0$ and an irreducible $σ_0$, so the Petersson norm is $\|F\|^2=t_μ\|c_F(μ)\|^2$ for all cusp forms $F$, with one $t_μ>0$, $μ$ the least exponent of $F_0$ and $c_F(μ)$ the coefficient of $q^μ$ in $F$. We prove that the harmonic weak Maass forms of weight $\frac12$ in the $σ_0$-isotypic part with a pole of least possible order are exactly the forms $\mathcal H_F$ with principal part $q^{-μ}\overline{c_F(μ)}$, and $ξ_{1/2}\mathcal H_F=F/t_μ$.
  For the four theta lattices it is a theorem that $t_μ=\frac{s-1}{12}\sqrt s$, with $s$ the square-free part of $|\det L|/2$, and the $\mathcal H_F$ come from umbral moonshine. For the eight others we compute $F_0$, $t_μ$ and $\mathcal H_{F_0}$: the Hecke eigenvalues are integers and, at the primes computed, the $a_p$ of an elliptic curve, and for three of the eight $F_0$ is explicit as an eta-theta product.
  We prove, for every prime $p>3$, a closed formula in $p$ and one class number for the difference $g(X_0(4p)/w_p)-g(X_0(2p)/w_p)$ of the genera of two Atkin-Lehner quotients of modular curves. In a family $\mathcal D_p$ of discriminant forms, $p$ an odd prime, containing three of the eight, comparison with that classification shows that $\mathcal D_p$ is rigid exactly when $X_0(4p)/w_p$ has genus $1$ and $X_0(2p)/w_p$ has genus $0$.

title: Archimedean Asai Zeta Integrals and Cohomological Test Vectors
summary: We construct explicit test vectors in the minimal $U(n)$-types of cohomological principal series representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb C)$, together with Schwartz functions, for which the Flicker zeta integrals equal the corresponding Asai $L$-factors. Both the vectors and the Schwartz functions are independent of $s$, with all normalization constants given explicitly. We construct the vectors through a polynomial realization of Schur modules. Schur orthogonality reduces the Flicker integrals to Mellin transforms of Whittaker functions, and Godement sections yield a recurrence for their Jacquet integrals. The lower-rank vectors depend on the remaining integration variables, preventing a direct reduction to lower-rank Flicker integrals. We overcome this difficulty by combining growth estimates derived from the recurrence with the Asai functional equation. This proves that the holomorphic quotient of the Flicker integral by its Asai $L$-factor is constant. An explicit asymptotic calculation shows that this constant is exactly one.

title: The Categorical Fargues-Scholze Correspondence at Generic Parameters
summary: Let $G$ be a quasi-split reductive group over a finite extension $F$ of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We study the Fargues-Scholze categorical Langlands correspondence at generic parameters $φ$, namely those whose semisimplification does not coincide with that of any parameter with nontrivial monodromy. Extending the theory of quasi-exceptional sets on the nilpotent cone developed by Bezrukavnikov to the setting of disconnected reductive groups which arise as stabilizers of semisimple generic parameters, to any irreducible representation $ρ$ of such a group we construct sheaves labeled $\overline{\nabla}_ρ$, $\overlineΔ_ρ$, $IC_ρ$, and $δ_ρ$ on the moduli stack of L-parameters for $G$. Using forthcoming work of Hamann, Hansen, and Mann on geometric Eisenstein series compatibility, the (conjectural, in general) behavior of the correspondence at generous parameters, and the (conjectural, in general) agreement between Fargues-Scholze and classical semisimple L-parameters we prove that these sheaves correspond under the Fargues-Scholze functor to the sheaves $i_{b!}π$, $i_{b\sharp}π$, $i_{b\sharp!}π$, and $i_{b!*}π$ on $\text{Bun}_G$, where $π$ is a smooth irreducible representation with Fargues-Scholze parameter $φ$. As applications we prove t-exactness properties of the Fargues-Scholze functor specialized at a generic parameter, and that Hecke operators are perverse t-exact on the generic locus. We also construct and study foundational properties of Hecke eigensheaves at generic parameters, compute non-semisimplified Fargues-Scholze parameters on the generic locus, and construct a Fargues-Scholze-theoretic version of the BM-O bijection at generic parameters.

title: Parahoric Spherical Whittaker Functions
summary: Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field and let $K_μ$ be a standard parahoric subgroup of $GL_n(F)$. We express the diagonal values of normalized parahoric Whittaker eigenfunctions with trivial central character using blockwise Casselman--Shalika formulas with the appropriate modulus factor. Every irreducible generic Iwahori-spherical representation has a one-dimensional fixed space for a suitable parahoric, with no invariants under a strictly larger parahoric. The full Hecke character of this line determines the representation. We compute its adjacent-block Hecke eigenvalues and, under additional irreducibility hypotheses, obtain an explicit finite formula on every Bruhat cell using an opposite induced model, Whittaker-preserving intertwiners, and Demazure--Whittaker operators. We apply these formulas to local Rankin--Selberg integrals for $GL_n\times GL_1$ and for compatible parahorics in $GL_n\times GL_m$. In the latter case, the lowest Laurent coefficient and the equal-rank functional equation determine the integral. Explicit translations and rescalings then give test vectors for the local $L$-factor.
